## Context / Problem

AGENTS.md's "Module-size policy (when editing rebar itself)" section prominently documents the 800-LOC module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`) but says NOTHING about its sibling CI gate: the shrink-only C901 cyclomatic-complexity ratchet (`.github/complexity-baseline.json`, McCabe max-complexity 15, enforced by `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` as part of `make lint`).

The ratchet fails the build whenever a function gains NEW debt or grows PAST its recorded per-symbol ceiling. This is exactly the failure mode of routine work like adding a CLI flag or a guard clause (added branches -> increased complexity), so an agent that adds a couple of flags to an existing command (e.g. create_cli/edit_cli) hits it predictably. Because it is a structural gate the behavioral test oracle cannot see, an implementer/orchestrator only discovers it at pre-flight, forcing an unplanned behavior-preserving extraction pass.

Discovered while implementing story cef7 (bridge_project/repos create+edit flags): the flag/guard additions pushed create_core (23>21), create_cli (26>22), edit_core (24>21) past ceiling and made edit_cli (16) new, failing `make lint` although the change was under the 800 LOC cap and lint/typecheck were otherwise clean.

## Approach

Add a short paragraph to AGENTS.md's Module-size policy section (or an adjacent "Structural gates" note) surfacing the complexity ratchet next to the LOC cap: what it is, that it is part of `make lint`, that it is shrink-only (fails on new/increased debt, ceilings in `.github/complexity-baseline.json`, threshold 15 in pyproject `[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]`), that the fix is behavior-preserving extraction (never bumping the baseline), and how to inspect it (`ruff check --select C901 <file>` / `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`). Cross-reference from the rebar-implement skill's 'ship the constraints the oracle cannot see' step so implementer briefs quote it alongside the module-size limit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AGENTS.md surfaces the C901 shrink-only complexity ratchet in/next to the Module-size policy section, naming the gate command, the baseline file, the threshold source, and the extraction-not-baseline-bump remedy.
- [x] The note explains it runs under `make lint` and blocks CI like the module-size gate.
- [x] A one-line pointer is added so a reader knows how to census offenders (`ruff check --select C901`).
